The true form of the moulding edge is laid off in the body plan by a double process of rabatment of the double cant plane, first about the trace <math>\text{AB}</math> to bring it perpendicular to the sheer plan, and then about a normal to the sheer plan through <math>\text{A}</math> to bring it parallel to the body plan, in the following manner. Set off <math>\text{P}_2</math>, <math>\text{Q}_2</math>, <math>\text{R}_2</math> on the middle line of the body so that their distances from <math>\text{A}_2</math> are equal to <math>\text{AP}</math>, <math>\text{AQ}</math>, <math>\text{AR}</math> measured along the trace <math>\text{AB}</math> in the sheer plan. Draw <math>\text{AC}</math> in the sheer plan perpendicular to <math>\text{AB}</math> and measure the heights parallel to <math>\text{AB}</math> of the points <math>p</math>, <math>q</math> and <math>r</math> above <math>\text{AC}</math>. Draw level lines <math>1\text{L}'</math>, <math>2\text{L}'</math>, <math>3\text{L}'</math> in the body plan at distances above the base line equal to these heights, and from the centres <math>\text{P}_2</math>, <math>\text{Q}_2</math>, <math>\text{R}_2</math> describe circles cutting <math>1\text{L}'</math>, <math>2\text{L}'</math>, <math>3\text{L}'</math> in <math>p_2</math>, <math>q_2</math>, <math>r_2</math>, &c., so that the radius <math>Q_2q_2</math> is equal to <math>\text{Q}'q'</math>, &c. The curve <math>p_2q_2r_2</math> is the true form of the moulding edge of the double cant laid off in the body plan.

The plane of the bevelling edge is parallel to that of the moulding edge and at a perpendicular distance from it suitable for use as the base of a bevelling triangle similar to that which is described for the ordinary frames.
